ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Sigmund Freud

text.paragraph: Mr. Freud is a 74-year-old physician and writer, seven years after a right partial maxillectomy for squamous cell carcinoma of the palate, with tobacco use disorder in early remission, who comes for his subsequent annual wellness visit five weeks after his twelve-week review and two weeks after the sick visit for Candida stomatitis. The burning has gone and the white patches have cleared; he now brushes the obturator and leaves it out at night. He has not smoked for ten weeks. He finished the 14 mg patch today as planned and keeps varenicline 1 mg twice daily and a few lozenges a day. His pain is 2 of 10 on acetaminophen. His weight is 60.2 kg. His remaining question is whether he should have a scan of his lungs. [S]

tr.td: No smoking for ten weeks; patch finished today; varenicline continues

Varenicline 1 mg twice daily, nicotine 4 mg lozenge as needed, acetaminophen 1,000 mg three times daily

list.item:
Subsequent annual wellness visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the written screening schedule updated. Lung cancer screening was discussed in detail: the USPSTF criteria count cigarette pack-years, and he smoked cigarettes only briefly, but about fifty years of heavy cigar smoking with some inhalation carries a real lung cancer risk, he has had a smoking-related cancer, and he is fit for treatment. He understood the possible benefit, false positives and radiation, and chose screening. One-time aortic aneurysm screening is recommended for men 65 to 75 who have smoked. [S]
Low-dose CT of the chest.
Ultrasound of the abdominal aorta.
Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines today.

Candida stomatitis (B37.0). Healed after nystatin and better prosthesis hygiene; no area of concern. [S]
Nystatin finished; continue nightly cleaning and leaving the obturator out at night.

Tobacco use disorder, severe, in early remission (F17.290). Ten weeks without smoking. [S]
Patch stopped today as planned; continue varenicline to complete at least 24 weeks and lozenges as needed.

Raised LDL cholesterol with a high cardiovascular risk (E78.5). Estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk over 20% after fifty years of smoking, with an LDL of 126 mg/dL; after discussion he chose a statin. [S]
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily; ALT and symptoms at the next visit.

Guideline basis: Initiating Pharmacologic Treatment in Tobacco-Dependent Adults. An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline (2020); Medicare Preventive Services reference: visit templates, screening cascades, and documentation elements (2026); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026); Lung Cancer: Screening (2021); Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: Screening (2019); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026)

Follow-up: Low-dose CT and aortic ultrasound in two weeks. Five-month review in four weeks with blood count, albumin, kidney function and ALT. Next wellness visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-26: five-month review: abstinence, lung and aortic screening results, pain, weight and the survivorship plan. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, and a health care proxy form was completed; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is being able to think, read and work, and that he would not want treatment that only prolongs suffering when work and thought are no longer possible. He asked for good pain relief if his cancer ever returns. No specific treatment orders were recorded today. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
